paper.title: Nonlinear Gravitational Memory in the Post-Minkowskian Expansion
paper.abstract: We present the first computation of the nonlinear gravitational memory waveform for the scattering of two compact objects in general relativity at leading order in the post-Minkowskian expansion. We use the scattering-amplitude-based representation of the gravitational waveform, which naturally expresses the nonlinear memory as the contribution of soft gravitons emitted by the gravitational waves themselves. We perform the calculation by applying a multipolar decomposition to the waveform and using the reverse unitarity method to obtain explicit exact-in-velocity predictions. We validate the results by calculating the corresponding velocity-expanded post-Newtonian multipoles, finding perfect agreement. Our results complete the knowledge of the gauge-invariant nonanalytic-in-frequency part of the <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mi>O</mml:mi><mml:mo>(</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mi>G</mml:mi><mml:mn>3</mml:mn></mml:msup><mml:mo>)</mml:mo></mml:math></inline-formula> multipolar waveform, thus providing a useful benchmark for future calculations of this quantity.

paper.title: Gravitational Waves from Feebly Interacting Particles in a First Order Phase Transition
paper.abstract: First order phase transitions are well motivated and extensively studied sources of gravitational waves (GWs) from the early Universe. The vacuum energy released during such transitions is assumed to be transferred primarily either to the expanding bubble walls, whose collisions source GWs, or to the surrounding plasma, producing sound waves and turbulence, which source GWs. In this Letter, we study an alternative possibility that has not yet been considered: the released energy gets transferred primarily to feebly interacting particles that do not form a coherent interacting plasma but simply free-stream individually. We develop the formalism to study the production of GWs from such configurations and demonstrate that such GW signals have qualitatively distinct characteristics compared with conventional sources and are potentially observable with near-future GW detectors.

paper.title: Impostor among Neutrinos: Dark Radiation Masquerading as Self-Interacting Neutrinos
paper.abstract: Multiple cosmological observations hint at neutrino self-interactions beyond the standard model, yet such interactions face severe constraints from terrestrial experiments. We resolve this tension by introducing a model where active neutrinos resonantly convert to self-interacting dark radiation after BBN but before CMB epoch. This exploits the fact that cosmological observables cannot distinguish between neutrinos and dark radiation with the same abundance and free-streaming properties. Our mechanism, based on a simple type-I seesaw framework along with a keV scale scalar mediator, achieves two objectives: (i) it produces strongly self-interacting dark radiation that imitates neutrino self-interactions favored by cosmological data, and (ii) it depletes the active neutrino energy density, relaxing cosmological neutrino mass bounds and easing the tension with neutrino oscillation data. The model naturally evades laboratory constraints through suppression of the neutrino-mediator coupling by the squared mass ratio of active and sterile neutrinos. We show that this scenario is favored over <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>Λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>CDM</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:math></inline-formula> by the combined Planck and DESI data, while being consistent with all other constraints. Our mechanism is testable in future laboratory probes of absolute neutrino mass and searches for sterile neutrinos.

paper.title: Gravitational-Wave Induced Freeze-In of Fermionic Dark Matter
paper.abstract: The minimal coupling of massless fermions to gravity does not allow for their gravitational production solely based on the expansion of the Universe. We argue that this changes in the presence of realistic and potentially detectable stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds. We compute the resulting energy density of Weyl fermions at 1-loop using in-in formalism. If the initially massless fermions eventually acquire mass, this mechanism can explain the dark matter abundance in the Universe. Remarkably, it may be more efficient than conventional gravitational production of superheavy fermions.

paper.abstract: Understanding whether primordial black holes form during strong first-order phase transition (FOPT) is a crucial open question in cosmology. We address this using a fully covariant formalism to study cosmological perturbations, highlighting previously overlooked gauge dependencies. We show that non-covariant treatments can overestimate primordial black holes and scalar-induced gravitational waves. Once gauge dependencies are accounted for, both signals are strongly suppressed, with direct implications for the FOPT interpretation of the Pulsar Timing Array signal.

paper.title: Ultraheavy Ultrahigh-Energy Cosmic Rays
paper.abstract: We investigate the propagation of ultraheavy (UH) nuclei as ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs). We show that their energy loss lengths at <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mo>≲</mml:mo><mml:mn>300</mml:mn><mml:mtext> </mml:mtext><mml:mtext> </mml:mtext><mml:mi>EeV</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:math></inline-formula> are significantly longer than those of protons and intermediate-mass nuclei, and that the highest-energy cosmic rays with energies beyond <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mo>~</mml:mo><mml:mn>100</mml:mn><mml:mtext> </mml:mtext><mml:mtext> </mml:mtext><mml:mi>EeV</mml:mi></mml:math></inline-formula>, including the Amaterasu particle, may be UH-UHECRs. For the first time, we derive constraints on the contribution of UH-UHECR sources, and find that the current data are consistent with energy generation rate densities of UHECRs from collapsars and neutron star mergers. Our model predicts that the mean value of the depth of shower maximum is lower than that for iron nuclei beyond 100 EeV, which can be tested with future composition measurements, e.g., AugerPrime and the Global Cosmic Ray Observatory. In addition, the spectral tension between the Telescope Array (TA) and the Pierre Auger Observatory can be alleviated by considering the enhanced contribution of UHECRs---including UH nuclei---from a nearby transient.

paper.title: Neural Post-Einsteinian Test of General Relativity with the Third Gravitational Wave Transient Catalog
paper.abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) from compact binaries are excellent probes of gravity in the strong- and dynamical-field regimes. We report a test of general relativity (GR) with the third GW Transient Catalog (GWTC-3) plus a few O4 events using the recently developed neural post-Einsteinian framework, both on individual events and at the population level through hierarchical modeling. We find no significant violation of GR and place a constraint that, for the first time, efficiently covers non-GR theories characterized by not only post-Newtonian deviations but also those beyond under the same theory-agnostic framework.

paper.title: Bifurcated Impact of Neutrino Fast Flavor Conversion on Core-Collapse Supernovae Informed by Multiangle Neutrino Radiation Hydrodynamics
paper.abstract: In this Letter, we present a compelling and robust argument for the roles of neutrino fast flavor conversion (FFC) in the explosion mechanism of core-collapse supernova (CCSN), combining the multiangle FFC subgrid model rooted in quantum kinetic theory with the multidimensional four-species Boltzmann neutrino radiation hydrodynamics. Employing various progenitor masses and the nuclear equations of states, we find that the effect of FFC on CCSN explosion is bifurcated depending on the progenitors. For the lowest-mass progenitor, FFC facilitates the shock revival and enhances the explosion energy, whereas for higher-mass progenitors its impact is inhibitory. We identify the mass accretion rate as the key determinant governing this bifurcation. When the mass accretion rate is low (high), the contribution of FFC to neutrino heating becomes positive (negative) because the heating efficiency enhancement via FFC-driven spectral hardening of electron-type neutrinos dominates over (is outweighed by) the concurrent reduction in neutrino luminosity. Our results further highlight the limitations of approximate neutrino transport and demonstrate that a multiangle treatment is essential for accurately capturing FFC effects; otherwise, FFCs are missed and even generated spuriously.

summary.title_zh: 中微子快味转换对核塌缩超新星的双重影响——基于多角度中微子辐射流体力学
summary.tldr: 首次在二维玻尔兹曼辐射流体力学中自洽耦合多角度快味转换子网格模型，揭示快味转换对超新星爆炸的影响随前身星吸积率呈双模效应：低吸积率时促进激波复活，高吸积率时抑制。
summary.highlight: 首次在二维多角度中微子输运框架下自洽实现快味转换子网格模型，无需引入自由参数；发现快味转换的双模效应由吸积率决定，低吸积率增强加热、高吸积率减弱加热；证明截断矩方法对快味转换的探测严重不足且可能产生虚假交叉，强调多角度处理不可或缺。
summary.authors_en: R. Akaho (Waseda University), H. Nagakura (National Astronomical Observatory of Japan), W. Iwakami (Waseda University) et al.
summary.context_outlook: 以往对快味转换（FFC）在核塌缩超新星中作用的探索多基于截断矩方法，因无法自洽判定转换发生，或手动预设转换区域，得到相互矛盾的结果（[[Ehring+ 2023]]），或尝试通过闭包重建角分布来推断，但重建方法被证明会低估甚至捏造电子轻子数交叉（[[Nagakura&Johns 2021]]、[[Nagakura+ 2021]]、[[Johns&Nagakura 2021]]、[[Cornelius+ 2025]]）。本研究在二维玻尔兹曼辐射流体力学中首次耦合多角度快味转换子网格模型，直接从角分布判断交叉并依据量子动理学（[[Zaizen&Nagakura 2023]]、[[Xiong+ 2023]]）确定渐近态，自洽揭示了快味转换对超新星爆炸的双重影响：在低吸积率前身星中增强中微子加热并促进激波扩张，而在高吸积率情形下抑制加热。结果强有力地表明多角度处理是准确捕捉快味转换效应的必要条件。未来仍需改进快味转换非线性演化的粗粒化模型，并纳入碰撞味不稳定性（[[Johns 2023]]）等效应，以更完整地理解中微子在超新星爆发中的作用。

paper.title: Scalar Fields around Black Hole Binaries in LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA
paper.abstract: Light scalar particles arise naturally in many extensions of the standard model and are compelling dark-matter candidates. Gravitational interactions near black holes can trigger the growth of dense scalar configurations that, if sustained during inspiral, alter binary dynamics and imprint signatures on gravitational-wave signals. Detecting such effects would provide a novel probe of fundamental physics and dark matter. Here, we develop a semianalytic waveform model for binaries in scalar environments, validate it against numerical relativity simulations, and apply it in a Bayesian analysis of the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA catalog. We obtain physically meaningful upper limits on scalar densities around most compact binaries. For GW190728 and GW190814, vacuum lies outside the 95% credible region. paper.title: Observable Gravitational Wave Strain at Second Order
paper.abstract: There is currently no rigorous definition of gravitational wave strain at second order in cosmological perturbation theory. The usual association of gravitational waves with transverse and traceless fluctuations of the metric on spatial hypersurfaces becomes ambiguous at second order, as it inherently depends on the spacetime slicing. While this poses no practical issues in linearized gravity, it presents a fundamental problem for secondary gravitational waves, especially notorious for gravitational waves induced by primordial fluctuations. We compute, for the first time, the observable gravitational wave strain at second order as measured by geodesic observers that emit and receive electromagnetic signals, thereby settling the debate on gauge ambiguities. Working in a gauge invariant fashion, we find that the measured gravitational wave strain coincides with the transverse-traceless components in the Newton gauge.

paper.title: Flexible Gravitational-Wave Parameter Estimation with Transformers
paper.abstract: Gravitational-wave data analysis relies on accurate and efficient methods to extract physical information from noisy detector signals, yet the increasing rate and complexity of observations represent a growing challenge. Deep learning provides a powerful alternative to traditional inference, but existing neural models typically lack the flexibility to handle variations in data analysis settings. Such variations accommodate imperfect observations or are required for specialized tests, and could include changes in detector configurations, overall frequency ranges, or localized cuts. We introduce a flexible transformer-based architecture paired with a training strategy that enables adaptation to diverse analysis settings at inference time. Applied to parameter estimation, we demonstrate that a single flexible model---called DINGO-T1---can (i) analyze 48 binary black holes from the third LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Observing Run under a wide range of analysis configurations, (ii) enable systematic studies of how detector and frequency configurations impact inferred posteriors, and (iii) perform inspiral-merger-ringdown consistency tests probing general relativity. DINGO-T1 also improves median sample efficiency on real events from a baseline of 1.4% to 4.2%. Our approach thus demonstrates flexible and scalable inference with a principled framework for handling missing or incomplete data---key capabilities for current and next-generation observatories.

paper.title: Black Hole Mergers Beyond General Relativity: A Self-Force Approach
paper.abstract: Gravitational waves from binary black hole mergers provide a glimpse of gravitational dynamics in its most extreme observable regime, potentially enabling precision tests of general relativity (GR) and of the Kerr description of black holes. However, until recently, numerical simulations of black hole mergers have not been possible in theories beyond GR. While recent breakthroughs have overcome that obstacle, simulations covering the full, interesting range of binary parameters remain unfeasible. Here we present a new first-principles approach to this problem. We show how self-force theory can be used to model the merger and ringdown of black holes in a broad class of gravitational theories, assuming one object is much smaller than the other. We calculate self-force effects on the merger waveform for the first time, and we demonstrate how our formulation allows us to modularly compute beyond-GR effects and readily incorporate them into a fast merger-ringdown waveform model.

paper.abstract: Repeated black-hole mergers in dense stellar clusters are a plausible mechanism to populate the predicted gap in black hole masses due to the pair-instability supernova process. These hierarchical mergers carry distinct spin characteristics relative to first-generation black holes. We introduce an astrophysically motivated model in the joint space of effective inspiral and precessing spins, which captures the dominant spin dynamics expected for hierarchical mergers. We find decisive evidence for a transition at <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>m</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:msubsup><mml:mrow><mml:mn>46.2</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mn>7.2</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>+</mml:mo><mml:mn>12.6</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msubsup><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>M</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⊙</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:mrow></mml:math></inline-formula>, above which the population is nearly entirely hierarchical, a location consistent with the anticipated onset of the pair-instability gap. We also infer a global peak in the hierarchical merger rate at <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>m</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:msubsup><mml:mrow><mml:mn>15.7</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mn>1.1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>+</mml:mo><mml:mn>3.2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msubsup><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>M</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⊙</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:mrow></mml:math></inline-formula>. The existence of low- and high-mass subpopulations of higher-generation black holes suggests the contribution of both near-solar-metallicity and metal-poor star clusters to the hierarchical merger population. Our results reinforce the growing evidence for detailed, mass-dependent substructure in the spin distribution of the binary black hole population.

paper.title: Signatures from Pion Condensation and Lepton Flavor Asymmetries in the Cosmological Gravitational Wave Background
paper.abstract: Large lepton flavor asymmetries at the QCD epoch could generate a pion condensation phase in the early Universe. For large enough tau lepton flavor asymmetries, the speed of sound can exceed the conformal value, leaving a distinctive imprint on the low-frequency gravitational wave (GW) spectrum from causal sources. Beyond probing the formation of a pion condensation phase, the detection or nondetection of this signature in future pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) datasets would provide a novel constraint on lepton asymmetries in the early Universe. We determine the corresponding GW spectrum and its tilt, comparing them with the standard case of vanishing lepton asymmetry. Finally, we discuss the implications for the stochastic GW background reported by PTAs, using the NANOGrav 15-year dataset.

paper.title: Collisionless Accretion of Finite-Angular-Momentum Plasma onto a Spinning Black Hole
paper.abstract: In low-luminosity active galactic nuclei like M87* and Sgr A*, the accretion disk around the central supermassive black hole is tenuous and collisionless. As a result, the usual ideal magnetohydrodynamics approximation may not be applicable. In this Letter, we report on the first fully kinetic simulations of the accretion process where the plasma initially has finite angular momentum, focusing on the case of axisymmetry. The simulated accretion flow behaves remarkably similarly to the magnetically arrested disk regime of ideal magnetohydrodynamics, reproducing episodes of magnetic flux saturation and eruption typical of magnetically arrested disks. The resemblance to fluid models owes largely to kinetic instabilities, which regulate pressure anisotropy in the disk, allowing fluid terms to dominate the angular momentum transfer. In addition, by handling vacuum regions effectively, our kinetic approach probes the matter supply to the jet funnel. We observe no efficient penetration of the accreting material into this region, suggesting that a pair discharge may be required to sustain the Blandford-Znajek process. These initial findings represent important groundwork to be checked and built upon by future kinetic accretion simulations, especially in 3D.

paper.title: The Trigger and Localization System of SVOM-GRM
paper.abstract: The Space multi-band Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) is an astronomical satellite jointly developed by China and France, primarily focused on the detection of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) and transient sources. The SVOM satellite was launched on 2024 June 22, with four payloads installed onboard. As one of payload, Gamma-Ray Monitor (GRM) comprises three gamma-ray detectors (each detector has an effective area of approximately 200 cm<SUP>2</SUP>) with distinct pointing directions, enabling the temporal and spectral measurements as well as localization of GRBs in the energy range of 15--5000 keV. This article first introduces the on-board localization algorithm design for GRM and presents preliminary test results. Then, leveraging abundant ground-based computational resources, a joint fitting method for spectral and localization analysis using Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) is implemented. paper.title: Study on the Detector Energy Response of SVOM/GRM
paper.abstract: The Space-based multi-band Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) mission is specifically designed to for the detection and localization of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) and subsequent follow-up observations. Among the four telescopes installed on the SVOM satellite, the Gamma-Ray Monitor (GRM) plays a crucial role in capturing the prompt emission of GRBs due to its wide field of view and broad energy range. Accurate determination of the detector's energy response is vital for analyzing GRM data, particularly considering the significant impact of the atmospheric albedo effect on this response. This research focuses on deriving the detector's energy response and establishing a calibration database for the GRM, with particular emphasis on investigating the atmospheric albedo effect. The study shows that the contribution of albedo photons to the detector's effective area depends strongly on the orientation of the Gamma-Ray Detector (GRD) line of sight (LoS) relative to Earth and on the incident direction of the GRB. When the GRD LoS is anti-Earth oriented, the albedo effect is minimal, with the highest proportion of albedo effective area accounting for approximately 10% of the total effective area. This occurs when the incident angle of the GRB is nearly perpendicular to the LoS. Conversely, if the GRD LoS is not pointing away from Earth and the GRB arrives from angles greater than about 90°, the albedo component can become predominant, contributing up to around 100% of the total effective area. This is especially pronounced in the 8--20 keV range, where the direct effective area drops to zero due to the large GRB injection angle. Our results show that, it is necessary for GRM to consider the atmospheric albedo effects in detector response, otherwise the spectral and localization analyses will result in biased measurements.

paper.title: GRM Scientific Pipeline
paper.abstract: The Gamma-Ray Monitor (GRM) is a key payload of the Space-based multi-band Variable Objects Monitor mission, which is designed to detect gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) within the energy range of 15 keV to 5 MeV. The GRM Instrument Center (GRM-IC) features real-time data processing through the X-band, enabling rapid response of high-energy GRB events. The system employs an event-driven architecture and distributed design, achieving efficient processing and real-time monitoring of massive observational data. Through comprehensive data production processes and scientific data product management, the system achieves efficient production of scientific data products of the L1B/C level through the submission of jobs to the task scheduling system. Through modular architecture design and automated processing workflow, the GRM data processing system realizes precise conversion and scientific analysis of GRB detection data, providing robust technical support for future system upgrades and cross-platform collaboration.

paper.title: SVOM/VT: Instrument Overview, Science Objectives, and First-year Performance
paper.abstract: The 44 cm Visible Telescope (VT) aboard the Space-based multi-band Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) is a dual-band (400--650 nm and 650--1000 nm) instrument designed to detect and characterize the optical counterparts of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) and other high-energy transients. This paper presents the VT's design, scientific objectives, observing strategies, and both space- and ground-based data processing pipelines, along with its first-year in-orbit performance. In-orbit commissioning tests confirm a sensitivity of 22.5 AB mag (300 s exposure), extendable to ~24 AB mag through stacking. This performance enables the VT to monitor over 100 GRBs in its first year with a remarkable ~80% detection rate for SVOM/ECLAIRS-triggered bursts and ToO-observed bursts from other missions (e.g., Swift, Fermi, Einstein Probe), outperforming Swift/UVOT's ~40% detection rate. Beyond its high detection efficiency, the VT played a key role in identifying high-redshift GRBs-most notably GRB 250314A (z = 7.3). Its deep upper limits at long wavelengths (up to 1 μm) were pivotal in guiding follow-up observations with large ground-based telescopes, enabling crucial near-infrared detections for this burst. With its rapid response, deep sensitivity, and real-time processing capabilities, the VT is a key instrument for GRB research in SVOM-era, enabling critical studies of GRB optical afterglows, circumburst environments, relativistic jet dynamics, and the origins of optically dark bursts.

paper.title: SVOM/VT: Flight Model Verification and Pre-launch Testing
paper.abstract: This paper presents pre-launch testing and calibration results for the Space-based multi-band Variable Objects Monitor, Visible Telescope Flight Model, validating its performance under simulated space conditions through thermal vacuum cycling, energy concentration analysis, stray light suppression, and CCD/electronics calibrations (gain, noise, quantum efficiency). The results confirm full compliance with design requirements: stray light suppression achieves point-source transmittance <10<SUP>-7</SUP> at 30° off-axis, thermal control maintains stable CCD temperatures (-75°C for the red channel, -65°C for the blue channel), and detection sensitivity meets the limiting magnitude of 22.50 (SNR > 3 with 300 s exposure). Early in-orbit tests further validate performance, yielding limiting magnitudes of 22.70 (V-band, red) and 22.78 (blue), consistent with pre-launch specifications.

paper.title: SVOM/VT: Preliminary Calibration Analysis
paper.abstract: We present the in-orbit calibration of the Visible Telescope (VT), one of the key instruments aboard the Space-based multi-band Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) mission for gamma-ray burst (GRB) studies. Using Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) as a reference, the VT achieves an astrometric precision better than 0<inline-formula> <mml:math><mml:mover><mml:mo>.</mml:mo><mml:mtext>″</mml:mtext></mml:mover></mml:math> </inline-formula>03 for bright stars, degrading to ~0<inline-formula> <mml:math><mml:mover><mml:mo>.</mml:mo><mml:mtext>″</mml:mtext></mml:mover></mml:math> </inline-formula>25 for faint targets. Shortly after launch, contamination was detected, reducing system transmission by ~40%. An initial bake-out successfully restored performance, but gradual recontamination caused transmission to decline by ~20% over the following 100 days before stabilizing. Despite this effect, routine standard star observations maintain precise zero-point calibration, ensuring photometric stability at the 0.02 mag level. Using synthetic stellar spectra, we derived photometric transformations to the Gaia, Sloan Digital Sky Survey, and Johnson--Cousins systems with typical residuals of 0.03 mag. These results demonstrate the VT system's capability and reliability in calibrating observations of GRBs and other transients.

paper.title: SVOM/VT: Overview of Data Processing and GRB Identifications with X-band Data
paper.abstract: The Visible Telescope (VT) is an optical telescope onboard the Space-based multi-band Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) mission, specifically designed to detect optical counterparts of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), study their afterglows, and select high-redshift candidates. It performs rapid follow-up observations simultaneously in two channels either via autonomous platform slewing or Target of Opportunity (ToO) observations. The science images acquired by VT and transmitted via the X-band downlink system are designated as VT X-band data. This paper provides an overview of GRB optical afterglow identifications with VT and describes the ground-based processing pipeline for VT X-band data, including preprocessing, astrometric calibration, and photometry. Up to 2025 December 3, VT has followed up 111 GRBs triggered by SVOM or external missions. The overall detection rate of optical counterparts is approximately 75%. Specifically, for bursts detected by SVOM/ECLAIRs, the detection rate is 77% when observed by VT within 30 minutes after the burst. A slightly higher detection rate of 81% is achieved for GRBs triggered by external missions through rapid ToO observations with a mid-time of less than 3 hr.

paper.title: SVOM/VT: Real-time Onboard Data Processing
paper.abstract: The Space-based Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) Visible Telescope (VT) is critical for the rapid identification of gamma-ray burst (GRB) optical counterparts, particularly for high-redshift candidates that require immediate infrared spectroscopic follow-up. To address the stringent bandwidth constraints of the Very High Frequency (VHF) downlink while ensuring real-time data availability, we developed the VT Onboard Data Processing Pipeline (VOPP). This paper details the software architecture, algorithms, and hardware implementation of VOPP using a Field-Programmable Gate Array and a CPU. The pipeline performs essential real-time tasks, including image quality assessment, dark and flat-field correction, and optimized image stacking to mitigate cosmic ray contamination and variable background noise. Furthermore, it generates compact source catalogs and highly compressed 1 bit images to facilitate rapid downlink. In-flight performance analysis confirms the pipeline's robustness, demonstrating the availability of VT VHF data for 78% of promptly slewed SVOM GRBs, with 56% leading to the identification of optical counterparts, typically within 18 minutes post-trigger.

paper.title: SVOM/VT: On-ground Processing of VT-VHF Data
paper.abstract: The VT--VHF data comprise three types of onboard-processed data results generated from four sequential observational sequences and transmitted to the ground via a Very High Frequency (VHF) downlink. On the ground, these data are processed by three successive pipelines: the pre-processing pipeline, the VT--VHF data processing pipeline, and the Visible Telescope (VT) afterglow candidate pipeline. These pipelines perform packet decoding, astrometric and photometric calibration, and afterglow candidate identification, respectively. This paper describes the architecture and operational implementation of the VT--VHF ground processing system and assesses its end-to-end performance using the first year of Space-based multi-band Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) operations. These data enable rapid identification of gamma-ray burst optical counterparts. Early detections, while the source is still optically bright, facilitate spectroscopic redshift measurements. Dual-band colors provide preliminary redshift constraints and help identify high-redshift candidates, whereas non-detections in both bands may indicate very high redshift, significant extinction, or intrinsically dark bursts. In-orbit operations show that the VT--VHF ground processing system successfully identifies optical afterglow candidates for a significant fraction of ECLAIRs triggers with available VT--VHF data, demonstrating its robustness and readiness.

paper.title: Overview of Ground-based Wide-angle Cameras Array
paper.abstract: As one of the key ground-based facilities of the Chinese--French Space-based multi-band Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) mission, the main scientific objectives of the Ground-based Wide Angle Camera array (GWAC) are to detect prompt optical emission of gamma-ray bursts or other short duration astronomical transients on a second-scale temporal resolution. GWAC is located at Xinglong Observatory, China, and consists of 10 mounts and 40 cameras, providing a joint field of view of about 3600 square degrees. The detection ability is 16 mag in 10 s of exposure time in the visual band under the condition of the new moon phase. Here, we give an overview of GWAC and introduce the science motivation of the project, as well as the performance of the hardware and the software. The observation strategies and the data processing are briefly presented. The early sciences in the last 5 yr since the first light are summarized.

paper.title: Alert Chain and Observation Planning for Ground Wide Angle Camera Network
paper.abstract: The Ground Wide Angle Camera Network (GWAC-N) is a robotic telescope network. It consists of ten wide-field core telescopes (GWAC-A) and two 60 cm narrow-field rapid follow-up telescopes (GWAC-F60A/B). The primary scientific goal of GWAC-N is to detect optical counterparts of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) discovered by the Space-based multi-band Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) satellite. This is achieved through synchronized monitoring with the GWAC-A array. Upon receiving a GRB trigger alert, the network conducts rapid, multi-band follow-up observations using the GWAC-F60A/B telescopes. The two-stage observation process involves many telescopes, making manual control impractical. Automated operations are therefore essential. They are realized through an integrated alert processing chain and an automated observation scheduling and dispatching mechanism. To enable this, we employ the SVOM Follow-up Observation Coordinating Service (FOCS) and GWAC-N's Automatic Observation Management (AOM) system. This paper presents the integrated alert processing workflow. It also describes the formulation of observation strategies, and the scheduling and execution of observations enabled by FOCS and AOM.

paper.title: SVOM/C-GFT: Instrumentation and Performance on the SVOM Alerts
paper.abstract: The Chinese Ground Follow-up Telescope is an optical facility upgraded to support the Space Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) mission. Located at the Jilin Observation Station, it is capable of rapidly identifying and monitoring the optical counterparts of gamma-ray bursts. The 1.2 m telescope is equipped with two switchable focal-plane instruments: the prime-focus Large-FOV Transient Imager with CMOS and the Cassegrain-focus Camera with Three Channels. In this paper, we present a system overview, including the observatory, the telescope, the instrumentation, the automated operational framework managed by the Operation Center, and the data processing pipelines. We also report the performance results obtained over one year of SVOM's post-launch operations. The results demonstrate that the system meets its design specifications and delivers robust observational and operational performance.

paper.title: COLIBRÍ (SVOM/FM-GFT): Instrumentation and Performances on the SVOM Alerts
paper.abstract: COLIBRÍ, the French--Mexican Ground Follow-up Telescope (FM-GFT) for SVOM, is a 1.3 meter rapid-response optical facility specifically developed for prompt, multi-band observations of GRB afterglows and for delivering sub-arcsecond localizations of optical counterparts for detailed follow-up studies. The telescope operates through a fully automated system that manages the entire workflow---from alert reception to counterpart identification. Commissioning results confirm that the telescope meets design specifications, and this paper presents a comprehensive performance assessment of the system's capabilities.

paper.title: The SVOM French Science Center Infrastructure
paper.abstract: At the heart of the Space-based multi-band Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) French ground segment, the French Science Center (FSC) is a cloud-based platform which provides services and tools for the management, storage, scientific processing and visualization of SVOM data for the French community. This digital center is a critical node of the SVOM system since it is the single point of access to SVOM scientific data for the French community and the only component of the ground system connected to the SVOM VHF network allowing near-real time communication from the satellite. Scientific processing pipelines are fully integrated into its infrastructure, allowing the automated production of high-level scientific data and the generation and broadcast of alerts to the scientific community at large. The software components of the FSC are running 24/7 and thus require a high level of automation, which led to the development of dedicated software relying on modern technical solutions such as micro-services, application containerization, infrastructure-as-code and continuous integration and deployment. In this paper, we describe the FSC infrastructure design, technological choices, and the process of SVOM data ingestion, archiving, and automated processing by the FSC scientific pipelines. We present analysis on the FSC performances in terms of availability, amount of data processed as well as processing speed.

paper.title: SVOM Science User Support at FSC
paper.abstract: The SVOM mission, a Sino-French collaboration dedicated to Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) and transient sources, began scientific operations in 2025. This paper describes the ground computing infrastructure and user support tools for SVOM's three observing programs: the Core Program (CP), the General Program, and Targets of Opportunity Program, the latter two being open to the broader scientific community, provided they collaborate with a mission Co-I. The mission adopts operational roles inspired by Swift, including on-duty scientists such as Burst Advocates, who validate GRB triggers and coordinate follow-up observations, and Instrument Scientists, who calibrate and validate data for all programs. Users can access observation schedules, public data products, and support tools via the French and Chinese mission centers. The SVOM portal serves as the primary interface for accessing these resources, including a GRB public table, API, and user documentation. This paper serves as a guide for both newcomers and external researchers interested in SVOM scientific operations, focusing on aspects related to the CP.

paper.title: SVOM Science User Support Services at Chinese Science Center
paper.abstract: The Chinese-French Space-based multi-band Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) mission is dedicated to the study of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) from the distant universe. A key component of the SVOM Chinese Ground Segment, the Science User Support Services (SUSS) provide comprehensive support for the mission's scientific operations. SUSS consists of two integral pillars: a suite of specialized software tools that automate key workflows, and a dedicated User Support Team that delivers expert-led, human services. These human-delivered services include operational coordination across telescope networks, direct technical assistance to astronomers, user training, and proactive problem-solving throughout the observation lifecycle. This paper focuses on the organization of SVOM scientific operations and the role of SUSS in facilitating these tasks. We provide a detailed description of the SUSS software architecture and its functionalities, encompassing the General Platform, the Burst Advocate support tools for GRB counterpart identification, the Target of Opportunity support tools, and the General Program support tools. The structure and services provided by the user support team at the Chinese Science Center are also elaborated. Furthermore, we evaluate the performance of SUSS during its first operational year, assessing its effectiveness in fulfilling user requirements. The evaluation offers valuable insights to guide future user support strategies and software enhancements, ultimately enabling better service for the SVOM scientific community.

paper.title: First Gamma-Ray Burst Observations with SVOM
paper.abstract: Following its launch on 2024 June 22, the Space-based multi-band Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) successfully completed its flight acceptance, commissioning, and scientific validation phases in early 2025, during which several tens of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) were detected onboard. Three quarters of these events have also been detected by other satellites, and a quarter are SVOM-only GRBs. In this article, we describe these early GRB observations, with a first description of the SVOM GRB sample that is emerging, and of the level of characterization already achieved, and with a focus on a few events of particular interest. These early results are very encouraging regarding SVOM's ability to detect and fully characterize (including prompt emission, afterglow and distance) a wide range of GRBs (classical long GRBs, short GRBs, X-Ray flashes, etc.) and to enable the use of these extreme high-energy transients as probes of the distant Universe.

paper.title: Early Results from the SVOM Observatory Science Program
paper.abstract: We present the organization and early results from the Observatory Science program of the Space-based multi-band Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM), based on data collected between 2024 July and 2025 December. Although primarily designed for gamma-ray burst studies, SVOM's wide-field, multiwavelength instruments enable a broad range of high-energy astrophysical investigations. We summarize the execution and performance of the General Program and Target-of-Opportunity observations, and we describe the frameworks used for serendipitous source detection and monitoring with the ECLAIRs coded-mask instrument. Over this period, SVOM carried out more than a thousand pointed observations and detected several hundred non-GRB high-energy sources, mainly X-ray binaries, as well as blazars, stellar flares, magnetars, and unidentified events. We highlight some key results, including the monitoring of the microquasar Cygnus X-1, the detection of burst oscillations from the low-mass X-ray binary 4U 0614+091, the spectral-state monitoring of Aql X-1, the first SVOM detection of an X-ray blazar flare from 1ES 1959+650, and observations of a stellar flare from HD 22468. These results demonstrate SVOM's strong capabilities for time-domain astrophysics beyond its core GRB program.

paper.title: The statistical properties of the cross spectrum
paper.abstract: The cross spectrum encodes the correlated variability between two time signals. In recent years, the cross spectrum has been used to study astronomical sources, particularly in the field of X-ray timing. In the literature, it has been common to either simultaneously fit the real and imaginary components of the cross spectrum, or fit the phase and magnitude. Until now, a full discussion of the statistical distribution of the cross spectrum has been missing from the astronomical literature. In this paper, we present a derivation of the full statistical distribution of a cross spectrum between two time series, showing that it follows an asymmetric Laplace distribution. We further provide the probability distribution function for a cross-spectrum random variable, along with the marginal distributions for many quantities. We also relate the cross spectrum to the power spectra of the constituent time series. This work will enable the cross spectrum to be used more accurately as a probe of physical processes such as accretion onto black holes and neutron stars.

paper.title: High-energy emission from the Galactic Center
paper.abstract: The center of the Galaxy is a prominent source in x-rays and gamma rays. The study of its high-energy (HE) emission is crucial to understanding the physical phenomena taking place in this dense and extreme environment, where the closest supermassive black hole (SMBH) to us, Sagittarius <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi>A</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mo>⋆</mml:mo></mml:msup></mml:math></inline-formula>, is lurking nearly invisible today in most of the energy spectrum. These phenomena are probably common to other galactic nuclei and may explain the feedback processes between nuclear regions and galaxies, which are so important for the overall evolution of the Universe. The Galactic Center HE emission is complex and consists of both thermal and nonthermal radiation produced by compact and extended sources, surrounded by more diffuse components. All these objects and media are interacting with each other in the narrow and dense Central Molecular Zone (CMZ). Some of them also show relevant extensions toward the Galactic poles, indicating energetic outflows that seem to link the center to the recently observed large Galactic polar structures. In spite of the fundamental advances obtained over the past 25 years with the most sensitive x-ray and gamma-ray observatories, several questions remain open to investigation. The main observational results and the open issues on the high-energy diagnostics of the Galactic nuclear activity are reviewed, with a focus on processes that take place in the CMZ, and, in particular, a discussion on the role of present and past SMBH activities in powering this region and possibly the entire Galaxy.

paper.title: CASPER: Interpretable gravitational-wave signal classification with a lightweight ResNet and FastSHAP explanations
paper.abstract: Classifiers for gravitational-wave strain data that are both interpretable and computationally accessible remain an active area of research in spite of matched filtering continuing to be the statistical gold standard for modeled signals. Although deep-learning classifiers have been shown to offer high sensitivity levels, many of these classifiers rely on computationally expensive architectures and provide limited interpretability at high computational cost. We present CASPER --- Classification with Attribution via ShaPley in Residual neural networks --- an interpretable binary classifier. CASPER combines per-prediction interpretability via FastSHAP, CPU-only deployability, a lightweight ResNet architecture, training on real GWOSC strain without synthetic injections, and an event-level evaluation protocol. Concretely, CASPER combines: (i) lightweight seven-layer ResNet CNN classifier trained on real GWOSC strain without synthetic injections; (ii) FastSHAP pixel-wise attribution maps that localize the time--frequency features responsible for each prediction within a single forward pass; (iii) Platt-calibrated output probabilities validated by Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Brier score; and (iv) CPU-only inference at 34 ms per segment. Evaluated on a held out set of 66 GWOSC events (7250 spectrograms, event-level split, no data leakage), CASPER yields mean event AUC = 0.906 (Segment level : 95% CI: [0.899, 0.914]) with Brier score = 0.099, outperforming a simple (non-residual) CNN baseline (mean event AUC = 0.864) trained under identical preprocessing conditions. FastSHAP attribution maps recover the inspiral chirp morphology and respond faithfully to pixel masking with reduced faithfulness at low SNR, consistent with the classifier's use of physically meaningful signal features which serves as input for classifier. The full list of GWTC event identifiers assigned to the training and test sets will be released with the code and trained weights via a permanent GitHub + Zenodo repository upon acceptance.

paper.title: Exploring the transitional parameter space of blazars using gamma-ray and X-ray population diagnostics
paper.abstract: We investigate the γ-ray and X-ray population properties of changing-look blazars (CLBs) using sources from the Fourth Fermi LAT Source Catalog Data Release 4 (4FGL-DR4) together with X-ray information from the Living Swift XRT Point Source (LSXPS) catalog. The CLB sample is compared with large populations of confirmed BL Lac objects (BLLs) and flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs) using spectral, variability, and broadband properties. In the γ-ray parameter space, CLBs mainly occupy intermediate and overlap regions between the BLL and FSRQ populations. However, the centroid locations in different parameter planes, along with the PCA and UMAP projections, show that the CLB population lies closer to the FSRQ region. The X-ray analysis also shows a similar behavior, where the overall distribution of CLBs in the X-ray parameter space is found to be nearer to FSRQs than to BLLs. In addition, the X-ray/γ-ray coupling relations and random-forest classification probabilities are consistent with this trend. Overall, the results suggest that CLBs form a transitional population between the two main blazar subclasses while retaining characteristics closer to the FSRQ population.

paper.title: Accretion and neutrino-motivated thermal diagnostics of thermodynamically reconstructed black holes from three-parameter generalized entropy
paper.abstract: We study accretion and thermal diagnostics motivated by neutrino processes for a static black hole reconstructed from a three-parameter generalized entropy. The construction is thermodynamic by design: the entropy deformation is not mapped to a radial-coordinate redefinition or to a prescribed Reissner--Nordström-like correction. Instead, the generalized entropy fixes the horizon response factor <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:msub><mml:mstyle><mml:mi>Ξ</mml:mi></mml:mstyle><mml:mi>h</mml:mi></mml:msub><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mi>d</mml:mi><mml:msub><mml:mi>S</mml:mi><mml:mi>G</mml:mi></mml:msub><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mo>/</mml:mo><mml:mi>d</mml:mi><mml:mi>S</mml:mi><mml:mo>|</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:msub><mml:mi>S</mml:mi><mml:mi>h</mml:mi></mml:msub></mml:msub></mml:mrow></mml:math>. The effective exterior geometry is then reconstructed by requiring its surface-gravity temperature to reproduce the generalized thermodynamic temperature. As a result, the metric preserves the horizon area and the Schwarzschild asymptotics, and reduces smoothly to Schwarzschild when Ξ<SUB>h</SUB> --> 1. The entropy response is encoded in <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:msub><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>G</mml:mi></mml:msub><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn><mml:mo>/</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mstyle><mml:mi>Ξ</mml:mi></mml:mstyle><mml:mrow><mml:mi>h</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math>, whereas the exterior radial dependence requires an additional localization prescription. The detailed accretion analysis is performed for the power-law family <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>h</mml:mi><mml:mrow><mml:mo>(</mml:mo><mml:mi>x</mml:mi><mml:mo>)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mi>x</mml:mi><mml:mrow><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mi>p</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup></mml:mrow></mml:math>, with p >= 2. Within this reconstruction family, positive λ<SUB>G</SUB> moves the photon sphere and ISCO inward, decreases the critical shadow scale, raises the radiative efficiency, and concentrates the energy release toward the inner disk, while negative λ<SUB>G</SUB> produces the opposite trend. A complementary comparison with exponential and rational localization functions shows that this qualitative ordering is preserved for the profiles tested, although the magnitude of the strong-field shifts remains profile dependent. Finally, the neutrino-motivated thermal sector is modeled conservatively using dimensionless temperature moments instead of a full neutrino-dominated accretion flow or annihilation-deposition calculation. The hierarchy among the <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>4</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math>, <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>6</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math>, and <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>9</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math> moments reveals that entropy-induced disk deformation becomes increasingly apparent with higher temperature exponents. Thus, within the adopted reconstruction framework, generalized entropy fixes the horizon response, while the exterior localization prescription determines how this response is propagated into compact-orbit and thin-disk observables.

paper.title: Circumstellar disc and X-ray variability in the Be/X-ray binary SXP 5.05 during its 2024 outburst
paper.abstract: Be/X-ray binaries provide a unique opportunity to study the interaction between neutron stars and circumstellar discs. SXP 5.05 is a particularly rare system, exhibiting eclipse-like X-ray variability attributed to obscuration by the Be star disc rather than a simple stellar eclipse. Motivated by its unusual geometry and the well-studied 2013 outburst, we present a multiwavelength analysis of its 2024 outburst using NICER X-ray observations and long-term optical monitoring from OGLE. The X-ray light curve shows a declining outburst with lower peak intensity and shorter duration compared to 2013, indicating a reduced accretion episode. The spectral evolution, characterized through hardness ratios, reveals a transition from a soft, high-intensity state to a harder, low-intensity state. Coherent pulsations near 5.05 s are detected throughout the observations, with properties consistent with previous measurements. The optical light curves show a reduced variability amplitude relative to 2013, possibly from a less extended or less dense circumstellar disc. Orbital-phase-folded optical profiles reveal a persistent, phase-locked dip structure, indicating a stable non-axisymmetric disc component that evolves across outburst phases. Together, these results support a picture in which the observed variability is driven by changes in disc structure and viewing geometry. SXP 5.05 thus remains a key system for probing the time-dependent properties of Be star discs through combined X-ray and optical observations.

paper.title: Classical long gamma-ray bursts as multimessenger sources: Recent developments in gamma-rays, neutrinos, and cosmic rays
paper.abstract: The status of classical high-luminosity long gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) as candidate sources of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) and high-energy neutrinos has changed substantially since 2019, and it has changed on three fronts more or less simultaneously. We restrict attention to that population throughout; the low-luminosity and hidden populations, on which the recent constraints bear far more weakly, are discussed only where recent results bear on them. A very-high-energy (VHE, <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>E</mml:mi><mml:mo>≳</mml:mo><mml:mn>100</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math> GeV) class of GRBs has been established by H.E.S.S., MAGIC, and LHAASO, culminating in GRB 221009A, for which the onset of the TeV afterglow was resolved and photons up to <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mo>~</mml:mo><mml:mn>13</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:math> TeV were recorded. IceCube has converted the absence of GRB neutrinos into quantitative bounds, both through stacked searches over thousands of bursts and through burst-specific limits on GRB 221009A. The Pierre Auger Observatory and the Telescope Array have consolidated a mass composition that grows heavier above the ankle, with a narrowing <mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>X</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>max</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math> dispersion, and Auger has reported evidence, at the <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mo>~</mml:mo><mml:mn>4</mml:mn><mml:mi>σ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:math> level, for an intermediate-scale anisotropy towards the Centaurus region, compatible with several nearby galaxy catalogues including starbursts. This focus review covers these developments and the constraints they place on one another, rather than the GRB field as a whole. These constraints apply to physically distinct regions: the TeV photons are afterglow emission from the external forward shock, whereas the neutrino limits and the Fermi-LAT cascade bound constrain the prompt dissipation zone, and the site of nuclear acceleration and escape is a model assumption in both cases. We therefore map each constraint onto its zone before combining anything. Within a single zone the compactness that governs photomeson production also governs photodisintegration and internal <mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:math> opacity, so transparency, neutrino faintness and nuclear survival are not independent; across zones no such implication holds without a model linking the prompt and afterglow flows. What the recent measurements do show is a convergence: analyses of different zones, by different methods, favour the same corner of parameter space, namely large radii and high bulk Lorentz factors, with the prompt-zone limits additionally requiring low baryonic loading. We summarize the resulting picture, which applies to co-spatial one-zone models of classical long GRBs and leaves multi-zone, reverse-shock, low-luminosity, and choked-jet configurations largely untested, together with the systematic uncertainties that currently limit it and the observations with CTAO, IceCube-Gen2, KM3NeT, GRAND, and AugerPrime that would test it.

paper.title: General Spin-1 Dynamics During Inflation: Microcausality Constraints and Cosmological Collider Signals
paper.abstract: We construct the general theory of a spin-1 field propagating on an inflationary background consistent with scale invariance, rotations, Bunch-Davies conditions and microcausality. Our Boostless Proca theory generalises the usual massive Proca theory to a Lagrangian with 5 free parameters: 4 corresponding to parity-even terms and a single parity-odd term. We impose three degrees of freedom from the outset and find that microcausality, the statement that field operators vanish outside the lightcone, requires the kinetic terms to be gauge invariant. We couple this spin-1 state to the inflaton and study the signatures it imprints on cosmological correlators. We find no new signals for the bispectrum meaning that the known signals are the most general thereby providing a very clean model-independent probe of new physics in this leading form of non-Gaussianity. For the trispectrum and higher-point functions, the boostless Proca theory produces new shapes with all 5 parameters in principle measurable.

paper.title: On the notion of kinetic energy in a spacetime of maximal proper acceleration
paper.abstract: It is shown in this work that in spacetimes of maximal proper acceleration there are situations where a particle decelerates and simultaneously increases its kinetic energy. To illustrate the effect, a classical $1$-dimensional electric cavity-like scheme is discussed. The gain in kinetic energy by deceleration suggests an equivalence between velocity and acceleration from the energetic point of view. Such an equivalence is stated in a form resembling Born reciprocity principle but formulated in the framework of higher order jet spacetime geometry. We also show the existence in the theory of a dynamical superluminal sector for point particles with positive mass and characterized by superluminal speed and a proper acceleration larger than the maximal proper acceleration. Therefore, the speed of light and the maximal proper acceleration become only {\it separation conditions} at the classical level of the two dynamical sectors.

paper.title: Quasi-periodic oscillations in Letelier black holes within Kalb-Ramond gravity embedded in a uniform external magnetic field
paper.abstract: We investigate the dynamics of charged test particles around a Letelier black hole, i.e. a black hole surrounded by a cloud of strings (CoS), in Kalb-Ramond (KR) gravity, immersed in an external, asymptotically uniform magnetic field aligned with the symmetry axis. The geometry depends on the CoS parameter and on the Lorentz-violating KR parameter only through a single combination of the two, so that the two effects can compensate each other and the Schwarzschild metric is recovered when both parameters are equal. Because the spacetime is not Ricci flat, the Wald potential is not a solution of the Maxwell equations; we show that the regular source-free magnetic test field is given in closed form by a Gauss hypergeometric function of the radial coordinate, which reduces to the Wald solution in the Schwarzschild limit. Using this exact field we derive the equations of motion, the effective potential, the circular orbits, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), representative escaping, captured and curled trajectories, and the orbital, radial and vertical epicyclic frequencies in closed form; all frequency expressions are cross-checked against direct numerical integration of the full equations of motion. Within the relativistic precession model, we perform a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis of the twin-peak high-frequency quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) of GRO J1655-40, XTE J1550-564 and GRS 1915+105 for four nested models, complemented by nested sampling to compute Bayesian evidences and to weight the two (Larmor and anti-Larmor) magnetic modes of the posterior. The Schwarzschild model is excluded for GRO J1655-40 and XTE J1550-564, with a difference in the Akaike information criterion of about 110.

paper.title: Lattice Monte Carlo of $λφ^4$ on Euclidean de Sitter
paper.abstract: We report the first Monte Carlo simulation of quantum field theory on Euclidean de Sitter space, $S^4$. Rather than discretizing space, we use a spectral lattice based on spherical harmonics, keeping all symmetries exact at finite cutoff. For a massless $λφ^4$ theory, the zero-mode distribution reproduces the Starobinsky-Yokoyama equilibrium at weak coupling, and deviations closely follow the one-loop renormalization of $λ$. At strong bare coupling, the renormalized quartic coupling saturates near the ceiling of the one-loop renormalization-group flow. This saturation is the de Sitter counterpart of the triviality mechanism that bounds the Higgs mass in flat space. Our results confirm nonperturbatively that the infrared divergences of light scalars in de Sitter are correctly resummed by the stochastic formalism. More broadly, this work opens up de Sitter space to lattice Monte Carlo methods.

paper.title: Proving the OSV conjecture with the gravitational path integral
paper.abstract: The OSV conjecture relates the helicity supertrace of black holes in $4d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity obtained through a Calabi--Yau compactification of Type IIA string theory to the modulus squared of the topological string partition function evaluated at the attractor point in moduli space for a given set of magnetic black hole charges and electric chemical potentials. We find Euclidean black hole saddles that compute this index to all orders in the 4d supergravity derivative expansion and calculate their action using equivariant localization. The gravitational on-shell action localizes entirely to the north and south poles of each black hole, with the two contributions determined by the holomorphic and anti-holomorphic topological string free energies, respectively, evaluated at the attractor values of the moduli. For single-center black hole saddles, this provides a proof of the OSV conjecture to all orders in the topological string coupling. The same localization formula also applies to all saddles that contribute to the helicity supertrace, such as multi-center black holes, which leads to a non-perturbative refinement of the conjecture.

paper.title: A Burst of Reionization in the Dark Ages
paper.abstract: Primordial overdensities at small scales can be significantly larger than those observed at large scales. As a result, they can collapse much earlier, at redshifts $z \sim 100$. In these collapsed halos, stars and black holes can form, where they can then contribute to an early reionization of the universe. If this epoch is temporary, the free electrons will recombine yielding a low level of ionization leading into cosmic dawn. This contributes to the optical depth of the universe, and adds more weakly to low-$\ell$ polarization signals of ionization compared to later sources. We study the effects of a redshift-localized source of reionization $Δτ_{burst}$ in the context of a broad suite of cosmological data to constrain this scenario, finding a preference of approximately $\sim 2-2.5σ$ for a new contribution. Regardless of Planck reprocessing used (PR3 - SRoll2+plik or PR4 - LoLLiPoP+CamSpec/HiLLiPoP), the results are consistent, favoring a new contribution $Δτ_{burst} \sim 0.012$ ($0.001 < Δτ_{burst} < 0.022$ at 95\%) and a similar total optical depth $τ\sim 0.073$. The precise era of reionization is somewhat discrepant depending on the higher-$\ell$ reprocessing used, with HiLLiPoP favoring $z\sim 45$, CamSpec $z\sim 100$ and plik $z\sim 165$. If such a source is present at $40\lesssim z\lesssim150$, LiteBIRD should be able to detect it, while Simons Observatory should also constrain it.

paper.title: Asymptotic AEther Misalignment and Universal-Horizon Mechanics
paper.abstract: Universal horizons trap even arbitrarily fast signals, providing a test of black-hole thermodynamics in theories with a preferred time direction. In Einstein--aether theory, this direction is defined by a dynamical field, the aether, that can remain non-aligned relative to stationary time at infinity. In particular, for asymptotically anti-de Sitter black holes, it was so far impossible to recover a first law of black-hole mechanics when such asymptotic tilt of the aether is present. Here, we resolve this issue for an exact family of static, spherically symmetric solutions. Using the covariant phase-space formalism, we identify the asymptotic tilt and the decaying part of the aether field as a boundary source and its conjugate response. Allowing both to vary independently obstructs the definition of an energy that generates time translations. Fixing either quantity, or imposing a relation between them, restores such an energy, while externally varying the boundary data introduces work into the first law. The energies obtained by fixing the source or its response are related by a Legendre transformation. At the universal horizon, heat includes both the metric area contribution and an irreducible aether energy flux. The resulting balance separates work at infinity from horizon heat and explains why the physical temperature cannot generally be inferred from the coefficient of an area variation in the black-hole mass.

paper.title: The accretionally heated atmospheres of protoplanets and brown dwarfs
paper.abstract: The ranks of accreting planets and brown dwarfs are growing. To help interpret their spectra, we study how accretion affects a planet's atmosphere. The atmosphere is irradiated from above by whatever nonthermal radiation from the accretion shock does not directly escape into space. This accretional heating drives a temperature inversion. Even relatively slow accretion, corresponding to mass doubling times longer than system ages, can raise temperatures by many hundreds of Kelvin at ambient pressures of order millibars. The heated atmosphere radiates an optical/infrared excess. For environments that are not too dusty, the excess concentrates in molecular lines that trace the heated layer. Thus an accretionally heated atmosphere may be distinguished by its muted absorption bands. Irradiation from the accretion shock also changes the chemical composition of the atmosphere, further altering spectra. Atmospheric retrievals promise to map out the deposition of accretional energy, helping to decide between ''hot'' and ''cold'' start modes of planet formation.

paper.title: Seeing in the Dark: Gravitational Waves from Resonant Production of Dark Photon Dark Matter
paper.abstract: Ultralight dark photons (DPs) are well-motivated dark matter candidates. A promising yet underexplored mechanism for their relic abundance is parametric resonance in the Abelian-Higgs model that generates the DP mass. We advance previous analytical studies through dedicated 3D lattice simulations that capture important nonlinear effects, including backreaction and relic partitioning between the dark Higgs and DPs. We further predict the associated stochastic gravitational-wave (GW) signal, which can be within reach of a broad range of detectors, opening a new avenue to probe ultralight DP dark matter.

paper.title: The road to $H_0$, $Ω_m$, and $w$ with a global neutrino-telescope network
paper.abstract: The newly measured correlation between the neutrino and X-ray luminosities of Seyfert galaxies has yielded the first neutrino-based measurement of the Hubble constant. Building on this result, we forecast the reach of a global neutrino-telescope network by 2030, utilizing full-sky IceCube exposures combined with KM3NeT-ARCA and Baikal-GVD. We find that this 2030 configuration sharpens the neutrino-measured Hubble constant from today's $H_0 = 66^{+44}_{-37}$ to $H_0 =66^{+15}_{-13}$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$. Additionally, we project that the disk-corona slope of the neutrino X-ray luminosity relation ($L_ν\propto L_X^β$) will reach $β=0.72\pm0.04$, enabling a $\geq \!5σ$ exclusion of the calorimetric value $β=1$. Finally, we show that, if a high-redshift population of neutrino sources, such as JWST's "little red dots," is identified and obeys the same luminosity relation, we can obtain a new independent measurement of the matter density $Ω_m$ and the dark energy equation-of-state parameter $w$.

paper.title: Nailing down the Hubble constant value through time delay cosmography: A 3% measurement from SN Refsdal
paper.abstract: We present the first inference of the Hubble constant and matter density parameter from a strongly lensed supernova (SN) by exploiting the mass model of a galaxy cluster enhanced by an extended surface brightness reconstruction. This has resulted in the most precise H0 measurement from a single strong lens so far, outperforming the 3.9% result from the lensed quasar DES J048-5354. Building upon the mass model of MACS J1149.5+2223 relying on image positions only, we incorporate the surface brightness distribution of the SN Refsdal host, to infer some cosmological parameter values within a flat LCDM framework. We consider two cosmological parameterizations, with either H0 and $Ω_m$ or H0 alone treated as free parameters. We explore four different mass-model realizations to assess some of the systematic uncertainties associated with the constraint weighting and source reconstruction. Although known as one of the main systematic effects, we deliberately keep the cluster total mass parametrization fixed to that of the previously published point-like mass model to enable a fair comparison. This reveals that incorporating 77,000 HST pixels reduces the uncertainty on the inferred value of H0 by a factor of 2.0. Our final measurements are $H_0=65.0^{+2.0}_{-1.8}$ km/s/Mpc and $Ω_m=0.30^{+0.08}_{-0.09}$, in agreement with previous results from lensed SNe. This corresponds to a substantially improved precision, reaching a remarkable 3.0% uncertainty on the value of H0. The contributions of the uncertainties on the lens total mass and on the measured time delays to the final H0 error are now comparable, indicating that future improvements will depend on more precise time-delay measurements and continued control of systematic effects. With sub-percent time-delay values reachable at cluster-scale, this mass model approach has the power to lead to unprecedentedly precise H0 measurements.

paper.title: "Mega-Earths" are likely an artifact of stellar activity
paper.abstract: Empirical relations and planet formation simulations suggest an upper mass limit for rocky planets of $\sim$10M$_{\oplus}$, as cores above this will almost certainly undergo runaway gas accretion. Nevertheless, a small number of planets appear to have densities consistent with rocky Earth-like compositions above this threshold, indicating that unusual formation and evolutionary scenarios are capable of producing extremely massive rocky planets called "Mega-Earths." However, all of these planets orbit active stars with log$R'_{HK}$ $>$-4.75. We find a <1$\%$ probability that all literature ultra-massive rocky planets would coincidentally orbit such active stars, and find no astrophysical reason to expect Mega-Earths to preferentially form around active stars. We therefore conclude that Mega-Earths are artifacts of stellar activity, and we question the reliability of Gaussian Processes to enable mass measurements for rocky planets around active stars.

paper.title: The Fast & Fourier: Using neural operators to speed up radiative modeling of protoplanetary disks
paper.abstract: Edge-on protoplanetary disks provide a spatially resolved view of the vertical distribution of icy planetary building blocks, but inferring their relative abundances requires radiative-transfer (RT) modeling with multiple anisotropic scattering. Each model costs $10^{1}$-$10^{3}$ CPU hours, which precludes principled Bayesian inference and homogeneous, population-scale analyses. We develop and validate a fast and reusable surrogate for Bayesian inference with ice-bearing edge-on disk models. We train a Fourier Neural Operator on a grid of RADMC-3D spectra. The network maps disk parameters and analytic physical input fields to the spectrum, using mixed-resolution spectra. We use the surrogate in an explicit-likelihood nested sampler and validate it on held-out simulations and synthetic recovery tests with TARP coverage. Finally, we use it to retrieve the disk structure and ice abundances of ESO-H$α$ 569 from its spectral energy distribution. The surrogate reproduces the RADMC-3D spectra with a median error of 4.84%. We recover synthetic parameters without detectable bias and with nominal coverage. For ESO-H$α$ 569, the posterior favors a massive ($M_{\rm gas}=0.028^{+0.015}_{-0.011}\,M_\odot$), nearly edge-on ($i=79.8^{+5.2}_{-2.4}$ deg) disk consistent with the image-plus-SED model of Wolff et al. (2017). Its ice abundances and cavity size remain weakly constrained by broadband data alone. The marginal spectrum-evaluation speed-up is $\sim10^{9}$-$10^{10}$. Neural-operator emulation makes full posterior inference feasible within the adopted model and training prior. Key posterior points should still be checked with high-fidelity RT models. By drastically cutting evaluation time, this approach enables for the first time homogeneous population studies of ices in disks, which new JWST surveys can capitalize on to map the range of compositions within planetary nurseries.

paper.title: Dynamics of Reheating in Modified Loop Quantum Cosmologies: mLQCI-I
paper.abstract: We study the reheating epoch and total bounce-to-present expansion in modified loop quantum cosmology using current observational determinations of the scalar amplitude and spectral index. We consider the power-law plateau potential, whose normalization is determined independently from the observed values of the scalar amplitude and spectral index. We find that, for the kinetic-energy-dominated initial conditions, the quantum-bounce regime is remarkably insensitive to this normalization, while the subsequent inflationary and reheating evolution shows a more appreciable dependence. We then investigate the sensitivity of the results to the inflationary potential by considering the Starobinsky and polynomial chaotic potentials. The reheating e-fold number and reheating temperature are found to depend strongly on both the form of the potential and, in the polynomial case, the branch selected. In contrast, the total bounce-to-present expansion satisfies the conservative bound N > 129 over the ranges considered here and remains close to the characteristic scale found in LQC. Moreover, the difference between mLQC-I and LQC is remarkably stable for all three potentials. These results suggest that reheating is strongly model dependent, whereas the small systematic shift in the total expansion is primarily associated with the different background quantum geometries of LQC and mLQC-I.

paper.title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
paper.abstract: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal peaks at $2k_c$ and has a sharp cutoff at this scale. We apply this result to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160 \mathrm{MeV}$ the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-$10 \mathrm{MeV}$ on such viable models.

paper.title: Bridging Theory and Observation: Synthetic Far-infrared Insights into Star Formation Efficiency
paper.abstract: The star formation efficiency per free-fall time ($ε_{\rm ff}$) quantifies how efficiently giant molecular clouds (GMCs) convert gas into stars and is often observed to be orders of magnitude lower than expected for free-fall collapse. Observers typically estimate $ε_{\rm ff}$ by mapping far-infrared (FIR) dust emission to infer gas surface densities ($Σ_{\rm gas}$) and counting embedded protostars, assuming simplified lifetimes and masses. Using the fiducial STARFORGE radiation-magnetohydrodynamics simulation of an $M_{\rm cl} = 2\times10^4 M_\odot$ GMC that self-consistently models star cluster formation and stellar feedback, we generate synthetic FIR observations and apply the same methodologies used in GMC surveys to investigate this discrepancy. We present the first $ε_{\rm ff}-Σ_{\rm gas}$ analysis in a fully feedback-regulated GMC simulation that resolves the formation of stellar systems. Our synthetic measurements reproduce the low observationally inferred efficiencies, showing that feedback-regulated star formation naturally produces $ε_{\rm ff} \sim 1-3\%$ without requiring extreme initial conditions. We also find that $ε_{\rm ff}$ varies strongly over a GMC's lifetime, suggesting that much of the observed scatter reflects evolutionary sampling rather than intrinsic cloud-to-cloud differences. Finally, by comparing observational and simulation definitions, we show that methodological assumptions introduce systematic biases, with a transition near $\log Σ_{\rm gas} \approx 2.3 M_\odot {\rm pc}^{-2}$ that depends on resolution. Above this threshold, the smoothing of dense structure increases both the inferred free-fall time and enclosed gas, with the latter dominating and suppressing $ε_{\rm ff}$. Below the threshold, the discrepancies are primarily driven by star formation rate assumptions.

paper.abstract: We convert existing exclusion limits on the elastic spin-independent (SI) dark matter--proton cross sections into upper bounds on the event rate, subsequently applying them to constrain other effective operators for inelastic scattering of light dark matter in the GeV mass region.
